tara: Noticing a small but consistent host CPU p95 bump on the new ingress patch. Initial flame shows tokenization + many small writev syscalls.
oscar: paste?
tara: condensed top paths:
```
tokenizer::batch_tokens_smallpayloads -> 21%
http::flush_per_request -> 19%
parse::header_machine -> 12%
kvcache::lookup_path -> 8%
net::writev_many_small -> 15%
```
li: looks similar to earlier small-write incidents. last change toggled aggressive-per-request flush for latency -> which set coalesce window to 0 for http1.
pat: kvcache dashboards show eviction spikes coincident with host CPU spikes (concurrent streams up). Could small writes be causing more connections/reconnects and hence cache churn?
perf-bot: quick diff: syscalls/writev +3.1x, connections short-lived +27%, kv eviction_rate +120% in the window.
tara: hypothesis: small writes -> higher syscall overhead -> higher CPU -> slower request completion -> higher concurrency -> kvcache churn -> more cache misses -> more CPU. feedback loop.
oscar: mitigation candidates: (1) restore a modest coalesce (2KB) for http1 unless client sets "no-coalesce", (2) bump tokenizer threadpool by +2 on canary, (3) add a micro-batcher to merge tokenization across tightly-timed requests, (4) kernel-selection nudge to prefer the "wide" kernel by slightly bumping batch size when queue depth high.
li: I ran a quick A/B: coalesce=2KB + tokenizer +2 threads -> p95 decode down 6%, CPU down 5%, writev rate -65%. partial win.
perf-bot: artifacts: s3://perf/6285000002/summary.json and CI job jobs/6285000002/short-profile.json.
pat: note on kernel selector: our runtime picks micro kernel for seq<=6 which has lower throughput per token. With the observed short sequences we frequently hit that slow path. If batching nudges median tokens >6 we get wide kernel.
oscar: can we implement a temporary adaptive nudger: if micro kernel fraction > 60% and queue_depth > 30, bump batch target +2 tokens for that host?
li: implemented prototype behind flag and ran tracegen (tools/tracegen --short --concurrency=200). Results: micro-kernel fraction dropped from 78% -> 25%, CPU p95 improved 8%, latency p95 improved 4%. No negative impact on tail for flagged tenants in the experiment.
tara: good. owners: I'll flip coalesce to 5% canary and own tokenizer pool experiment. oscar: you'll own kernel-nudge rollout. pat: watch kv dashboards and set alert if eviction spikes >1.5x baseline.
perf-bot: deploy-bot: ramped coalesce=2KB to 5% at t=6285000015; kernel-nudge flag at 5% at t=6285000016.
pat: after 30m: writev syscalls down 58%, kv eviction normalized, conn reuse up 18%. kernel-nudge pushed wide kernel selection on canary hosts.
li: follow-ups: (A) add header-based opt-out for coalesce for clients that require immediate flush, (B) add a metric for "kernel-selected" vs "median-batch-size" in dashboards, (C) prototype preparse micro-batcher but gate it behind tenant opt-in.
oscar: long-term: consider smarter kernel selector that looks at per-host recent sequence histogram instead of per-request.
tara: I'll draft a short postmortem with root cause + mitigation steps and link perf artifacts. leaving canary for 6h soak, will report final numbers. :eyes:
